Reaching out costs nothing and puts no obligation on you.

whyChoose.title: What You Should Know Before You Wait

items.title: The Clock Is Running
items.desc: California generally gives you two years from the date of injury to file a claim, but claims against a government entity can require action in as little as six months.

items.title: Fault Doesn't Have to Be All-or-Nothing
items.desc: Under California's pure comparative fault rule, you can still recover damages even if you were partly responsible for the crash — your share of fault just reduces the amount.

items.title: No Cap on What You've Truly Lost
items.desc: In ordinary injury cases, California places no cap on non-economic damages like pain and suffering, so your recovery isn't artificially limited.

items.title: Nothing Out of Pocket to Start
items.desc: We work on contingency, which means we only get paid if you win — there's no upfront cost to you.

items.question: How long do I have to file a claim in Montebello?
items.answer: In most California injury cases, you have two years from the date of the incident to file a lawsuit. If a government entity was involved, such as a city vehicle or road defect, the window can shrink to as little as six months, so it's worth checking sooner rather than later.

items.question: Where do crashes tend to cluster in Montebello?
items.answer: Public records show higher collision counts along corridors like SR-60, Beverly Boulevard, and Whittier Boulevard, with reports peaking on Fridays between 5 and 7 p.m. These are neutral traffic counts, not a judgment about any particular road.

items.question: What if I was partly at fault for the crash?
items.answer: California follows a pure comparative fault rule, so being partially at fault doesn't bar you from recovering compensation. Your total recovery is simply reduced by your percentage of fault.

items.question: Is there a limit on what I can recover for pain and suffering?
items.answer: No. California does not cap non-economic damages, like pain and suffering, in standard personal injury cases. This differs from some other states, so it's worth understanding your full options.

items.question: Does it cost anything to contact you?
items.answer: No. We offer free initial case reviews. Our team typically works on contingency, meaning no fee unless you recover money.
